response.query: What GLP toxicology group sizes, endpoints, and numeric go/no‑go toxicity thresholds will we set prior to initiating GMP/IND activities?
response.answer: For GLP toxicology, group sizes, endpoints, and toxicity thresholds are set based on regulatory guidelines, typically requiring at least three animals per group, specific organ toxicity endpoints, and no observed adverse effect levels (NOAEL) to determine go/no-go for GMP/IND activities.

results.content: In addition, applicants will collaborate with NIH-funded consultants and can augment their project with NIH contract research organizations (CROs) that specialize in medicinal chemistry, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, formulations development, chemical synthesis including under Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), and Phase I clinical testing. Potential applicants are strongly encouraged to contact NIH Scientific/Research staff prior to preparing an application to clarify which entry stage is most appropriate for their project and what to include in their plans for the UG3 preparatory phase. * For projects entering at the Development stage, evaluate if the applicant has a well profiled and fully optimized compound with in vitro and in vivo biological activity, as well as, ADMET properties appropriate for the intended clinical use. + For Discovery stage projects, evaluate whether there are any constraints of which that could impede their use of compounds, assays, or models for research purposes and/or commercial development (e.g., certain restrictions under transfer or sharing agreements, applicants' previous or present intellectual property filings and publications, compounds with similar structures that are under patent and/or on the market, etc.).
